title: As GTA 6 breaks records, Take-Two CEO says he isn't interested in an EA-style $55 billion buyout: "Additional scale doesn't seem to help"
summary: "We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive," says Strauss Zelnick

(Image credit: Rockstar) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Ahead of GTA 6 's launch, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick says there's no need for the company to go private like EA because it's already successful enough. Speaking on a new episode of Bloomberg's David Rubenstein show (below), Zelnick is asked if he has any interest in selling the Rockstar Games parent company like "two of the biggest competitors" in the business recently did – while they're not mentioned by name, EA and Activision Blizzard are almost certainly the competitors in question here. Clearly, though, that's not a consideration for the CEO. "I think we've proven that we can do very well as an independent company," he begins. "And now we're, you know, a rather large company. We're at scale, and we're at a point where we have a terrific balance sheet. At the end of this fiscal year, we should be a net cash company again. We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive." Latest Videos From GamesRadar+ Watch full video here: Strauss Zelnick on GTA VI, Take-Two's Turnaround and AI | The David Rubenstein Show - YouTube Watch On Certainly, GTA 6's imminent release will help there – it's the most pre-ordered game of all time on both the PlayStation and Microsoft stores, and one market intelligence firm estimated that it's already reached $942 million in revenue, even before launch. "In the entertainment business, scale matters once you aren't at a certain point," Zelnick continues. "Below about $1 billion in revenue, it's hard to field a competitive creative team, it's hard to field worldwide marketing and distribution, and it's hard to survive the inevitable flops that occur. But once you're well over $1 billion in annual revenue – and we're way beyond that point, our guidance is $8 to $8.2 billion this fiscal year – additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed." You may like With GTA 6 delays, Take-Two CEO suggests Rockstar didn't want a Cyberpunk 2077 situation With GTA 6 about to launch, Take-Two boss unloads on investor criticizing "years of delays" It's not just GTA 6 – Take-Two boss argues "we have the best collection" of IP in the business Zelnick is right to be confident – after all, he reckons that Take-Two has "the best collection" of IP in the games business , and between GTA, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock alone, it's hard to argue there. Acquisitions can bring in a lot of unwanted changes, too. Not long after EA was sold for $55 billion to Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners earlier this year ( taking on $20 billion in debt in the process ), it announced the closure of Dragon Age and Mass Effect studio BioWare, and canceled Mass Effect 5 . For fans of Take-Two and the studios it owns, then, it doesn't seem like a bad move to keep things as they are.
